Problem: Teachers need the same subject-first organization as students without a mixed-subject resource area.
Long-Term Behavior: Each teacher subject opens a self-contained workspace for resources, assessment, classes, analytics, communication and AI.
Key Requirements: Board → Qualification → Subject → CurriculumVersion context on every read/write; subject-scoped authorization.
Existing Feature Relationship: Extends F-164/F-165 and existing teacher module
Agent Notes: Canonical teacher product boundary; not a second curriculum.

Problem: Students enrolled by teachers need LMS features while retaining their normal adaptive-learning workspace.
Long-Term Behavior: Class-enrolled students receive Announcements, Assignments and My Results/Feedback inside the subject workspace; independent features remain available.
Key Requirements: Class membership overlay; same student identity; same learner state; backend authorization.
Existing Feature Relationship: Extends subject-first student architecture and F-070/F-071/F-075
Agent Notes: A student may simultaneously be independent and class-enrolled.

Problem: Class KG must distinguish not-yet-taught curriculum from taught-but-weak curriculum.
Long-Term Behavior: Store a separate teacher/class/subject teaching-coverage overlay; NOT_TAUGHT is not a mastery state.
Key Requirements: SpecificationPoint scope; class scope; timestamp; teacher provenance; auditability; no curriculum mutation.
Agent Notes: Grey graph nodes semantically mean absent teaching coverage, not low understanding.

Problem: Teachers need grounded help creating resources and understanding syllabus requirements.
Long-Term Behavior: Subject-scoped academic copilot for specification questions, question drafting, explanations, resource linkage and lesson preparation.
Key Requirements: Grounded retrieval; citations; model/provider/prompt metadata; generated content is draft until validation.
Existing Feature Relationship: Complements existing F-040 Tutor/KA-RAG and F-050 Test Builder
Agent Notes: Separate from Data Assistant; academic/content copilot, not learner analytics.

Problem: Teachers need natural-language answers about class and student evidence.
Long-Term Behavior: Authorized natural-language analytics for weak topics, weak specification points, mock marks, misconceptions, trends and affected students.
Key Requirements: Structured query/calculation first; LLM summarizes returned evidence; scope/time-window/freshness visible; no hallucinated stats.
Agent Notes: Example: Which topic is 10A weakest at? Why? What did Sara score in the latest mock?

Problem: Teacher Test Builder needs to exploit specification-point and learner evidence, not only topic/difficulty filters.
Long-Term Behavior: Enhance F-050 with SpecificationPoint, concept, skill, misconception, class weakness, teaching coverage and other evidence-backed filters while retaining manual selection, reuse/edit and PDF export.
Key Requirements: Validated question bank; explicit question provenance; review before assignment/publication; official vs generated distinction.
Existing Feature Relationship: EXTENDS F-050; do not duplicate Test Builder
Agent Notes: Save My Exams reference confirms topic/difficulty filtering, teacher-only questions, reuse/edit and print-ready PDFs.

Problem: Class heatmaps must lead to actionable student-level inspection.
Long-Term Behavior: Click class node → affected students → evidence distribution → individual subject graph → assessment/resources → teacher action.
Key Requirements: Same graph model/read model as student KG; teacher-authorized context; no second KG implementation.
Agent Notes: Class graph is an aggregation/lens over learner states.

Problem: Early-warning flags are not useful if teachers cannot inspect why a student was flagged.
Long-Term Behavior: Extend F-073 so every risk state shows contributing evidence, time window, rule/model version and uncertainty where applicable.
Key Requirements: Evidence-first; rule/model versioning; expert validation for research-sensitive thresholds.
Agent Notes: Never present an unexplained AI risk score.
